keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws Thessaly in the Greek City-States aggregate and then Macedon (-350). Neither page gives an area or the perioikic members; the gazetteer's Thessalia is the researcher's reading. Jason 'briefly transformed Thessaly into a powerful Greek state' and 'soon extended his control to much of the surrounding region', but the Jason page names no region (it explicitly names no power over Perrhaebi, Magnesians or Phthiotic Achaea).

region.text: Thessaly (the gazetteer's Thessalia, Greece); the perioikic peoples are not named on the pages

ledger.note: 374: Jason of Pherae unites Thessaly. 'By 374 BCE, the Pherae and the Aleuadae were united with the common, agricultural population of Thessaly by Jason of Pherae'; 'Jason strengthened the Thessalian League and made alliances with Macedon and the Boeotian League (374 BCE)'; the Jason page: 'appointed tagus, or chief magistrate, of Thessaly in the 370s BC'. The League itself is older (tagos, the four tetrads of Aleuas, undated).

region.text: Thessaly (the gazetteer's Thessalia, Greece); the perioikic peoples are not named on the pages

ledger.note: c. 353: Philip II takes Thessaly. 'His interventions eventually resulted in the defeat of the tyrants of Pherae around 353 BCE'; Philip 'was elected president (archon) of the Thessalian League' for life. Jason was assassinated in 370, Alexander II of Pherae died in the late summer of 358 ('opened a path for Philip's diplomatic conquest').

wars.name: Theban-Thessalian campaign against Alexander of Pherae
wars.outcome: 'In the year 364 BCE, the new joint Thessalo-Boeotian army, led by the Theban general Pelopidas, marched'; Alexander of Pherae 'ruled harshly before finally being defeated by the Thebans' (Jason page).
wars.note: No territorial change is on the pages; the League page gives the Pelopidas reorganisation (archon for tagos, the four tetrads) without a date.

sources.title: Thessalian League
sources.note: By 374 Jason unites Thessaly; 370 Jason assassinated; 364 Pelopidas; 358 Alexander II dies; c. 353 Philip defeats the Pheraean tyrants; archon for life; Rome 196.

sources.title: Jason of Pherae
sources.note: Tagus in the 370s, 'much of the surrounding region' unnamed, Epirus and Macedon relations, Heraclea in Trachis, assassination 370, successors.

notes: Written for eu-01-c's request ('Thessalian League and Pherae (Alexander of Pherae)'), covering Jason's state only to Philip II's takeover at about 353, because the pages date nothing else of territory. The League continues under Macedon and, from 196, as a Roman-sponsored koinon ('Rome established Thessaly as a koinon, Federal League', League page; 'leave the following peoples free' at the Isthmian Games of 196): a later extension for the Hellenistic groups. The League page puts the noble families' rise in the 5th century BC, against Jason's 4th-century context (possibly a page error). The Jason page says nothing of the c. 374 date, Perrhaebi, Magnesians, Phthiotic Achaea, Phocis or a formal Boeotian alliance. Counterparts: greek-city-states, macedonian-empire (Philip II), sacred-band-of-thebes (eu-01-c, -379..-362).
